stem: The daily sales (in units) recorded at a small shop over seven days are: 12, 15, 12, 18, 20, 12, 15. What is the mode of this data set?

per_option_rationale.rationale: The value 12 appears three times, which is more frequent than any other value (15 appears twice; 18 and 20 appear once each). Mode = most frequent observation.
15 appears twice but 12 appears three times; selecting 15 means using the second-most-frequent value instead of the true mode.
18 is neither the most frequent nor a central value; a student may pick the largest middle value, confusing mode with median position.
13.43 is the arithmetic mean (sum = 94, n = 7, mean = 94/7 = 13.43); a student who computes the mean instead of the mode arrives here.

explanation: Mode is the observation with the highest frequency. Tallying: 12 appears 3 times, 15 appears 2 times, 18 and 20 appear once each. The mode is 12.

explanation_sections.punchline: Frequency count reveals 12 appears three times, making it the unique mode.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the distribution model: mode = most frequently occurring value. Tally each distinct value: 12->3, 15->2, 18->1, 20->1. Pick the value with tally = max.
explanation_sections.lesson: Mode is the value with the highest frequency; it is not affected by extreme values or any arithmetic on the data.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 30 seconds. Eliminate option 4 first (it is a mean computation), then compare frequency of 12 vs 15.
